claim: A ceiling stated in processor seconds says nothing without the machine it was measured on, and the pool an audit lands in spans about 1.9 times in per-core speed. A number tuned on the fast node refuses on the slow one, and a number tuned on the slow node catches nothing on the fast one. The audit at 9ce258fc ran on node-05 and refused no-color-literal, manifest-names-what-is-reached, typecheck and tests-pass on their ceilings, and identifier-matches-its-place died on SIGKILL. By ceiling over usual cost those were the 4th, 5th and 8th lowest-headroom checks in the repository, at 1.88, 2.02 and 2.33, on a machine running the audit's own work about 1.9 times slower per core than whatever the earlier rounds ran on. Nothing about those checks changed: their readCalls matched the earlier rounds to within a tenth of a percent and their peak memory was unchanged.

evidence:
Measured on 2026-09-19 from the audit cost rows each check keeps beside its own page at check/code/pages/<slug>/<slug>.check-code.audit.logs.uncommitted.jsonl, and from the cluster.

The pool. jobFor in infrastructure/job/modules/cluster-running/cluster-running.module.code.ts picks nodes with workloadClassMemberSelector for the class ci, and four nodes carry that label. A pod run on each reads out of /proc/cpuinfo: node-01 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9700F CPU @ 3.00GHz, 8 processors; node-04 AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor, 12; node-05 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-3930K CPU @ 3.20GHz, 12, the only one of the four without avx2; node-06 AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor, 32. The i7-3930K is a 2011 part and the 5950X a 2020 one. A single-threaded integer loop in a pod held to one cpu, best of seven rounds, takes 9200 ms on node-05 against 5615 ms on node-06, a ratio of 1.64. The audit's own work runs wider, at 1.85; what carries the difference between a register loop and a parser is not measured here.

The episode. kubectl names node-05 for pod audit-9ce258fcace3-jj30dyww-8vlx5, the round at commit 9ce258fc, which ran from 08:38:42Z to 09:18:13Z. Four checks refused on their ceilings: no-color-literal spent 16.199 against 15, manifest-names-what-is-reached 28.236 against 25, typecheck 304.664 against 300, and tests-pass reported 12 test files over the 5 processor seconds a test file is given. identifier-matches-its-place died on SIGKILL, judging nothing.

The headroom. Taking each check's usual cost as the median of every earlier audit row its log holds, and its ceiling from the audit group on its own page, the lowest-headroom checks in the repository run page-matches-its-type 1.75, popover-keeps-its-viewport-cap 1.75, page-named-as-stated 1.78, no-color-literal 1.88, manifest-names-what-is-reached 2.02, no-code-comments 2.07, no-page-address-spelled 2.23, typecheck 2.33. Three of the four that refused are the 4th, 5th and 8th on that list. The round inflated every check about equally: over the 54 checks with enough earlier rows to compare, the round's cost against that check's own earlier median has a median of 1.85 and a mean of 1.89, which is a property of the machine and of no check. readCalls matched to within a tenth of a percent on every one, and peak memory was unchanged.

The comparison ranOver makes. ranOver in check/modules/run-ceiling/run-ceiling.module.code.ts adds cpuSeconds and childCpuSeconds off the cost row and weighs the sum against auditCeiling, a bare number on the check's page. Nothing in that weighing reads which machine either number came from. A ceiling set from rounds on node-06 leaves a check about 1.9 times over on node-05; a ceiling set from rounds on node-05 sits about 1.9 times above what the check ever spends on node-06, so it catches a real regression only after the check has doubled.

What is unmeasured. Nobody has shown from the cluster that the earlier rounds ran on node-06. KEPT_SECONDS in cluster-running sets ttlSecondsAfterFinished to 3600, so an audit Job and its pod are reaped an hour after they end, and only the round at 9ce258fc is still there to ask. That the earlier rounds ran on a faster node is an inference from the inflation of 1.85 over 54 checks whose readCalls matched, and from node-05 measuring slower than node-06 on a loop of its own. Which node any earlier round ran on is recorded nowhere. Cost rows carry the node from dec98a319a3 onward, so the next such episode is read off the row rather than inferred.

Neighbouring ground. a-test-files-processor-seconds-rise-with-the-machines-core-count has a processor-second ceiling moving with the machine too, by the compiler spinning one worker per core of whichever node it landed on. That one is more cores charging more for the same work; this one is slower cores charging more for the same work. Both leave a ceiling stated as one number meaning a different thing on each node of the pool.
